new.title: Wander the Crooswijk cemetery
new.desc: Opened in 1832 during a cholera outbreak, the Algemene Begraafplaats Crooswijk was laid out as a park open to all faiths. Weeping beeches and willows shade the graves of politicians, a wartime double agent and the composer of the Czech national anthem.
new.tip: Look for the Walloon Church memorial and the Commonwealth war graves; it is a calm, green walk a short tram ride from the centre.

new.title: Find the village inside the city in Overschie
new.desc: Overschie was its own village until 1941, and its Dorpsstraat still feels like it: the old Raedthuys and two churches line the street where four different waterways called Schie meet.
new.tip: Come on a Friday morning and add the neighbourhood market, held every week since 1958.

new.title: Find the castle ruin in a Hillegersberg churchyard
new.desc: In the middle of the Hillegondakerk graveyard, on the sandy rise that gave Hillegersberg its name, stand the remains of a 13th century castle tower that troops of Jacoba van Beieren destroyed in 1426.
new.tip: Walk on along the Straatweg between the two Bergse Plassen lakes, dug out by peat cutters centuries ago.

new.title: Spot the first gallery flat in the Netherlands
new.desc: The Bergpolderflat (1934) by Willem van Tijen with Brinkman and Van der Vlugt was the country's first true gallery-access block, built of prefab steel to keep rents low for workers. Its open galleries and glass stairwell became the model for decades of Dutch housing.
new.tip: It is a private residential building, so admire it from the street; combine it with a stroll through nearby Blijdorp.

new.title: See the Nederlands Fotomuseum in its new warehouse
new.desc: The national photography museum has moved into Pakhuis Santos, a listed 1902 coffee warehouse on the edge of Katendrecht, with a rotating line-up of shows from Dutch documentary greats to new talent.
new.tip: Combine it with a walk across Katendrecht to the Deliplein for dinner.

new.title: Slip into the Schoonoord garden
new.desc: Tucked beside Het Park, this garden goes back to 1706 and hides a pond, a botanical collection, birds and trees more than 250 years old. Few passers-by know the gate is open.
new.tip: It closes in the late afternoon, so make it a daytime stop before or after the Euromast.

new.title: Walk to the old quarantine station at Heijplaat
new.desc: On a strip of land along the Maas, the city once isolated sailors and emigrants with infectious diseases. The listed Quarantaineterrein is now home to artists, and the path beyond it ends at a rare natural sandy beach on the river.
new.tip: Take the waterbus to RDM and follow the 'Rondje Heijplaat' walk with its detour to the Quarantaineterrein.

new.title: Pay respect at the 'Ze Hielden Koers' memorial
new.desc: Next to the Erasmus Bridge, the colourful little park on the Leuvehoofd surrounds the memorial to the merchant seamen who kept sailing during the Second World War. It is also one of the best spots for sunset over the river.
new.tip: Come at golden hour and watch the ships turn under the bridge.
new.q: Monument Ze hielden koers, Leuvehoofd, Rotterdam

new.title: Stroll the Heemraadssingel
new.desc: This 1.5 kilometre canal park from around 1900 cuts through Rotterdam West, lined with grand houses, old trees, little bridges and artworks. It is the leafy side of the city most visitors never see.
new.tip: Start at metro Coolhaven and walk north to Beukelsdijk, then drop into Historic Delfshaven on the way back.

new.title: Learn the war story at Museum Rotterdam '40-'45 NU
new.desc: Museum Rotterdam's Second World War branch at the Coolhaven tells how the city lived through occupation, bombing and liberation, and why those years still shape it today.
new.tip: Visit before or after the 14 May commemoration to understand the fire line markers you see in the pavement.

new.title: Have a special beer at Café De Riddert
new.desc: A tiny brown café on the Mauritsweg with a long list of special beers and whiskies and the occasional live band. The beer casks sit under the floor, which opens up now and then right behind the bar.
new.tip: If the floor hatch opens, step back and enjoy the show.

new.title: Eat British pub food aboard Vessel 11
new.desc: A former British lightship moored in the Wijnhaven, one of the city's oldest harbours, now a gastropub with a seasonal British menu and beer from its own floating brewery, V11.
new.tip: In summer, grab a seat on the deck and watch the boats in the harbour.

new.title: Order house-made dim sum at Asian Glories
new.desc: A Michelin Bib Gourmand Chinese restaurant near the Binnenrotte, cooking Cantonese and Sichuan dishes with dim sum made in-house and roast ducks hanging in the open kitchen.
new.tip: Go with a group and share as many dim sum baskets as you can.

new.title: Taste wood-fired vegetables at Rotonde
new.desc: This lively vegetarian restaurant on the Goudsesingel cooks local vegetables over an open fire, think glazed celeriac with Dutch miso, and earned a Michelin Bib Gourmand for it.
new.tip: Come early for coffee and small bites at Bar Bocht next door.

new.title: Drink a fresh beer at Brouwerij Noordt
new.desc: A brewery and tasting room on the Zaagmolenkade by the Rotte, pouring around twenty of its own beers with a terrace on the water in Rotterdam Noord.
new.tip: Brewery tours run on Fridays and Saturdays; book one and finish on the terrace.

new.title: Dine in a 1597 inn at In Den Rustwat
new.desc: A thatched old inn in Kralingen with antique tiles and Delft Blue pottery inside and a terrace looking out over the Trompenburg arboretum. Michelin praises its refined cooking.
new.tip: Book a table for a special occasion and walk through Trompenburg beforehand.

new.title: Hang out at the Keilecafé in M4H
new.desc: What began as a pop-up in the old Merwe-Vierhavens port district grew into a permanent hangout for drinks, food, dancing and even yoga among the warehouses.
new.tip: Pair it with a walk over the Dakpark down the same street.

new.title: Grab a summer beer at Biergarten
new.desc: An open-air beer garden on the Schiestraat near Centraal Station, where Rotterdammers gather on long summer evenings for drinks and grilled food.
new.tip: Best on a warm weeknight after work; it fills up fast on Fridays.

new.title: Shop the Afrikaandermarkt
new.desc: The big neighbourhood market on the Afrikaanderplein reflects the area's dockworker and migrant history, with spices, fabrics, vegetables and snacks from all over the world. Feyenoord once played its home matches on this very square.
new.tip: It runs on Wednesdays and Saturdays; walk there from the Entrepothaven to see more of the neighbourhood.

new.title: Explore the island under the Van Brienenoord Bridge
new.desc: Right under the busiest bridge in the country lies a small river island with woods, open water, Highland cattle and allotment cottages. The traffic hums overhead, but the skyline view from the water's edge is worth it.
new.tip: Go by bike from the IJsselmonde side and bring a picnic.

new.title: Ride the historic tram line 10
new.desc: Volunteers of the Rotterdam public transport museum (RoMeO) run vintage RET trams on a hop-on, hop-off city loop past the Markthal, Delfshaven, the Erasmus Bridge and the Cube Houses.
new.tip: It runs at weekends in spring, summer and autumn, plus Thursdays and Fridays in summer; regular transport tickets are not valid, buy one from the conductor.

new.title: Go sailing on the Kralingse Plas
new.desc: The lake in the Kralingse Bos has its own sailing community, and you can rent a small boat and tack between the windmills and the forest with the skyline on the horizon.
new.tip: Boats can be rented at the sailing school on the Plaszoom; pick a day with a light breeze.

new.title: Lose yourself in the Zuiderpark
new.desc: At 215 hectares it is counted as the largest city park in the Netherlands: allotments, football fields, water and wide lawns stretching across Charlois, right behind Ahoy.
new.tip: Rent a bike and loop the whole park, it is bigger than you think.

new.title: Catch an indie film at KINO
new.desc: An independent cinema in the multicultural Oude Westen, showing arthouse and international films with a bar and restaurant to talk about them afterwards.
new.tip: Explore the shops and food of the Oude Westen before the screening.

new.title: Watch grain being milled at De Zandweg
new.desc: A brick corn mill from 1723 in Charlois, still grinding grain regularly thanks to volunteer millers. A surprising piece of village history in Rotterdam Zuid.
new.tip: Visit when the sails are turning; the miller is happy to show you around inside.
new.q: Molen De Zandweg, Kromme Zandweg 99, Rotterdam

fix.problem: The quest points to the Keilestraat brewery in M4H. Kaapse Brouwers opened a new brewery, De Kaai, on the Maas in May 2026 (a 2025 permit puts it at Nassaukade 3), and its original taproom is Kaapse Fenix in the Fenix Food Factory on Katendrecht.
fix.suggestion: Repoint to Kaapse Fenix, Nico Koomanskade 1025 (Katendrecht), area guney, coords about [51.9035, 4.4865]; drop the Keilewerf tip and mention the river terrace instead.

fix.problem: El Aviva on the Schiedamseweg had its kitchen gutted by fire in July 2024; I could not confirm it has reopened. The inventor, hairdresser Nataniël Gomes, died in 2023.
fix.suggestion: Verify El Aviva is open again; otherwise reword the tip to point to the Schiedamseweg in general (where Gomes' salon was) rather than one snack bar.

fix.problem: DutchReview notes the small Luchtpark garden on the Hofbogen is reportedly gone and a new 1.2 km rooftop park on the viaduct was due to start construction in 2025, so 'on top a park' may currently be a building site.
fix.suggestion: Soften the desc to say a rooftop park is being built on the viaduct; also consider area merkez, since the Luchtsingel starts at the Schiekade/Pompenburg edge of the centre.
